solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old chicken Joey beginning to marinate somewhere below deck

parts.note: a boiler is an older fowl, fit only for stewing or boiling
a joey is a young kangaroo, giving ROO

indicators.note: the beginning of the following word supplies just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A recipe: an old hen and a baby kangaroo, with the marinade just starting, prepared somewhere below deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' takes the M of 'marinate'. A joey is an Australian young kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship the engine and boiler space lies beneath the decks, so it is one place below deck.

clue.text: Produce eggs (value to change)

indicators.note: the words before it are asked to change, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A biology note: egg production, with a parenthetical aside about a value needing to change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges the letters of VALUE TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovaries release eggs during this process, so the verb means producing eggs in biology.

clue.text: Store acting to remove PG Tips

indicators.note: the following letters are to be taken away from the word just found

parts.note: acting on stage is playing
the tips, or ends, of the acting word are its P and G; PG Tips is also a British tea brand

explanation.surface: A shopper stocking up on tea: store away PG Tips, the British tea brand.
explanation.walkthrough: PG Tips is a well-known British brand of tea, but here the tips (end letters) P and G come off PLAYING.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay in supplies is to stockpile them, so the phrasal verb matches the verb store.

clue.text: Others back inside care facility

parts.note: the others are the rest
back home means returned indoors, so home stands for inside

explanation.surface: The other patients are back inside the care facility after an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A residential institution where elderly people live and are looked after is a care facility.

clue.text: Cheering, Son's pot shot makes it 1-0

indicators.note: shot here means wrecked or ruined, so the letters before it are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheering crowd as a son's shot at goal puts his team one up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like the son's attempt at goal but signals rearranging CHEERING, SONS and POT.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoring the first goal of a match changes the scoreline from nil-nil to one-nil.

clue.text: See 8
Very hot temperature leaves part of London noticeably steamy

parts.note: so means very, as in so hot

indicators.note: the temperature letter leaves, or departs from, the word hot

parts.note: taken as written before losing a letter

explanation.surface: A sweltering day makes one district of London noticeably steamy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noticeably steamy' nods to the district's racy reputation. Soho is a central London district known for nightlife and its former sex trade.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a district in the West End of the capital, famous for clubs and restaurants.

clue.text: Member of harbour staff to deserve representation

indicators.note: a representation of the words re-presents them, so their letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A dock worker seeking the union representation he deserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representation' rearranges TO DESERVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone employed to load and unload ships is one of the workers at a port.

clue.text: He supervises the key workers, allegedly

definitions.text: He supervises the key workers, allegedly

parts.words: He supervises the key workers, allegedly
parts.note: key sounds like quay, so the official in charge of a port's dock workers is described with a pun, flagged by allegedly

explanation.surface: A boss overseeing essential staff, as people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key workers' suggests essential staff, but it is said like quay workers, the people working at the waterfront.
explanation.definitionFit: The official in charge of a port oversees the dock and its workers, hence quay workers.

clue.text: Area of port property not lit

indicators.note: not lit means the letters of lit are left out of the word found

parts.note: a property of something is a quality it has

explanation.surface: Part of a harbour property with no lighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes LIT from QUALITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing place alongside which ships moor is one area of a harbour.

clue.text: A stressed, upset husband under arrest weeps

indicators.note: a person under arrest is held in custody, so the husband letter is held inside the rearranged letters
upset means knocked over, so the letters of the words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A stressed wife, upset because her husband has been arrested, weeps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges A STRESSED, and 'under arrest' places H inside that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Crying is letting fall drops from the eyes, so the phrase matches weeps.

clue.text: Inaugurate boat

definitions.meaning: to start or set up something new
a large motorboat or a ship's boat

explanation.surface: Launching a new vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to set going and a type of motor vessel, two senses of one word.

clue.text: Bob, going downhill rapidly, very bony appearance

definitions.meaning: a sled, like a bobsleigh, on which a rider goes head first down an ice track
a gaunt person looking all bones

explanation.surface: Bob is racing downhill and looks painfully thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name but is the sled; this is the winter sliding sport and its sledge.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a head-first sliding sled and the bony framework of the body, seen in someone emaciated.

clue.text: State speed when pursuing marine mythical creature

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so these pieces come after the marine piece

parts.note: marine means relating to the sea
NY is New York, a US state
speed is measured in mph, miles per hour

explanation.surface: A report of how fast something sped while chasing a marine monster.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nereid or other water spirit of legend is a female mythical being living in the ocean.

clue.text: Small blade (maybe 25) used by Spooner when out after dark?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: small in weight is light
a blade, perhaps the one at 25 across, is a knife

explanation.surface: A small knife, perhaps a famous one, that a clergyman carried on evenings out.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of LIGHT and KNIFE gives the sounds of the answer; the silent K means only sounds are swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubs, bars and entertainment enjoyed in the evening are what people do when out late.

clue.text: Monster therefore getting sent back

indicators.note: sent back means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: A monster is therefore being returned.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eating giant of folk tales is a monster.

clue.text: Low joist hampering new skylight?

indicators.note: hampering means enclosing and restricting, so the new letter is held inside the pieces

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
a joist is a beam

explanation.surface: A low joist gets in the way of fitting a new rooflight.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: a ray from the moon is light from the sky, not a window.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray shining from the moon is literally light in the sky, a witty twist on a roof window.

clue.text: German on hols working in the US as a port employee

indicators.note: working means being worked over and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A German on holiday takes a job in America at the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges GERMAN ON HOLS. 'in the US' warns that this is the American word for a dock worker.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a dock labourer loading and unloading ships is employed at a port.

clue.text: Gold coin tossed over river

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: a tossed coin is flipped about, so its letters are mixed up

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A gold coin flipped over a river, perhaps for luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossed' rearranges COIN.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the great waterway of Venezuela, a South American river.

clue.text: See 17
Fix a trial involving rising winger for hire

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
involving means containing, so the letters sit within the words

explanation.surface: Rigging a trial that involves a winger on the rise, as in football.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' is not a footballer: it is anything with wings, here a plane you can hire.
explanation.definitionFit: A small aircraft chartered for short trips is a winged craft available for hire.

clue.text: Pier worker, Australian, supporting daughter

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: an ocker is a rough, uncultivated Australian

explanation.surface: A dock worker from Australia supporting his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts OCKER below D in the down light. Ocker is Australian slang for a boorish Aussie.
explanation.definitionFit: A labourer at the docks works on piers and wharves.

clue.text: Returning inside, shoos out rival master

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters are read backwards
the letters needed sit inside the run of words

explanation.surface: Coming back inside, someone shoos a rival out.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert performer, especially a musician, is a master of their art.

clue.text: We recalled feeding police informer in Notts town

indicators.note: feeding means going into, so the letters sit inside the informer

parts.note: a nark is a police informer in British slang

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned

explanation.surface: We remember giving information to a police informer in a Nottinghamshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Notts is short for Nottinghamshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Newark-on-Trent is a market town in Nottinghamshire.

clue.text: Yorkshire river out east where vessels tie up

indicators.note: out means removed, so the east letter is dropped

parts.note: the Wharfe is a river in Yorkshire, northern England

explanation.surface: On a Yorkshire river, out east, boats tie up.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing structure where ships berth and load is where vessels are moored.

clue.text: With which to cut Kiwi beef on travels?

definitions.text: With which to cut Kiwi beef on travels?

indicators.note: travels means moving about, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: What a traveller might use to cut New Zealand beef while on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travels' rearranges KIWI BEEF ON, and the whole clue describes a large hunting blade a traveller carries.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sheath knife used for hunting would serve to cut meat on a journey.

clue.text: Norwegian group first to ban whaling captain

parts.note: a-ha was a Norwegian pop group

indicators.note: first to means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A Norwegian band is first to ban a whaling captain.
explanation.walkthrough: a-ha was a Norwegian pop band of the 1980s, famous for Take On Me.
explanation.definitionFit: The obsessive captain of the Pequod in Moby-Dick hunts the white whale.

clue.text: Cable starts to read old political epistles

indicators.note: the starts of the following words give their opening letters

explanation.surface: A telegram prompts someone to read old political letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cable' looks like a telegram, but it is a thick cord.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick strong cord used on ships is both a cable and a line.

clue.text: Revolting bad smell Ms Thurman? Fish? That'll be the urchin

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so all the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: niff is British slang for a bad smell
Uma Thurman is an American actress
a gar is a fish with a long beak-like snout

explanation.surface: A disgusting smell, an actress and a fish: that must be the street urchin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like disgust but turns NIFF, UMA and GAR back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragged, scruffy child of the streets is an urchin.
